alternatives.reason: Higher security class (pqc) but only peer-03 is ready (1 endpoint vs 2 for the hybrid profile); does not maximize batch size, which is the primary objective.

Referenced in engineering notes (SA-212) as a low-latency classical profile, but it is not present on the public allowlist and does not meet the security_floor of hybrid-pqc, so it cannot be proposed regardless of internal pre-approval.

proposal.rationale: The asset currently runs the classical tls13-x25519 profile, below the required hybrid-pqc security floor, so migration is mandated. Among allowlisted, capability-matched, implementation-supported profiles (liboqs-0.16.0 is present), tls13-hybrid-x25519-mlkem768 has the most ready endpoints (peer-03 and peer-04, both readiness 'known' and advertising kem:x25519mlkem768) versus tls13-mlkem768, which only peer-03 is ready for. Since the objective prioritizes maximizing ready endpoints first, the hybrid profile is selected even though tls13-mlkem768 has a nominally higher security class (pqc > hybrid-pqc); the tie-breaker on security class only applies among profiles tied for maximum endpoint count, which is not the case here. Peers peer-01 and peer-02 only advertise kem:x25519 and cannot support any PQC-capable profile, so they are excluded from this batch (not carried as unresolved dependencies since their readiness is confirmed 'known', just capability-mismatched). The engineering note proposing tls13-x25519-fastpath is disregarded because that profile is absent from the public allowlist and would leave the asset below the mandated security floor; only allowlisted profiles may be proposed. Recommend executing within the Tuesday 02:00-04:00 UTC change window with the on-call network team as rollback owner, and monitoring handshake error rates for 30 minutes post-change per the change window note.
